- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.1) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to capture mean reversion.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
- If sentiment is volatile or mixed (0.1–0.3), model exhibits lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 periods to align with sentiment momentum.
- In low-sentiment environments (sentiment <0.1), model underestimates downward trends; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast to avoid under-shock.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-period sentiment shifts; apply sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., last 3 sentiment values) to adjust final 5–7 days.
